llm.summary: The skill is mostly a disclosed Mapbox development guide, but it normalizes risky token handling and broad account permissions that users should review carefully.

dimensions.detail: The self-hosted configuration shows `MAPBOX_ACCESS_TOKEN` placed directly in persistent editor configuration, and project-local MCP config is described as committable without adequate warning about credential or endpoint exposure.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The hosted setup is disclosed and OAuth-based, but the Claude Desktop example runs unpinned `npx mcp-remote`; the self-hosted path requires cloning, installing, and building a Mapbox server package.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Several examples ask the assistant to create development tokens with all scopes or full access, which conflicts with the skill's own least-privilege guidance and is broader than ordinary style development requires.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill persists MCP server configuration in user or project editor files and can grant an assistant ongoing access to Mapbox account operations, including token and style changes, once configured.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The Mapbox MCP purpose is coherent with style creation, validation, documentation lookup, and token management, but the documented workflows include account mutation, token creation/listing, and style deletion without strong safety framing.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable giving your AI assistant development-time access to Mapbox account operations. Prefer OAuth hosted setup, pin any `npx` bridge package, avoid project-committed MCP configs for secrets, never paste real tokens into shared config files, and create narrowly scoped tokens instead of all-scopes development tokens.
llm.findings:
[PE3] expected: References to Mapbox access tokens and token tools are expected for a Mapbox MCP setup guide; the artifacts do not show credential-file theft or hidden token collection.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The plaintext `MAPBOX_ACCESS_TOKEN` configuration example, broad-token examples, and sparse warnings around sensitive token display are real documentation safety concerns rather than malicious behavior.
[RA2] expected: Project-local MCP configuration is a normal setup option, but users need clearer warning that these files persist and may be shared or committed.
[T08] unexpected: Using unpinned `npx mcp-remote` is not intrinsic to the skill's Mapbox purpose and creates mutable third-party code execution risk at assistant startup.
[T09] unexpected: The token placeholder in persistent editor configuration is not a leaked real secret, but it encourages a pattern that can expose real Mapbox tokens if copied directly.
[T05] unexpected: Examples recommending all-scopes or full-access development tokens are overbroad for routine Mapbox style work and materially weaken least-privilege controls.
